title: Fix the status-downgrade bug so a warning can never mask an error
objective: Stop a later check's status="warning" from overwriting an earlier check's status="error" in check_and_enable_services, which made genuinely broken services report as warnings and then never get repaired. Found while writing the split's tests and deferred out of 9085a4e5 because it changes live enforcement; the user asked for it to be fixed.
acceptance_criteria: No bare `status="warning"` assignment remains in any check lib; every one is guarded by `if [[ $status != "error" ]]`, matching the idiom already used in services_apps.sh and services_browser.sh.
A timer that is BOTH disabled and inactive records "error" and triggers its setup script, demonstrated by an A/B run against a simulated broken machine rather than only by assertion.
The regression is covered by tests that FAILED before the fix and pass after it.
Every file including the test files stays at or under 250 lines.
shellcheck reports zero findings and no suppression is added.
out_of_scope: The 5 sites that were already correctly guarded.
Changing which statuses report_and_fix acts on: the fix makes the status correct rather than widening the repair gate.
The kcov attribution artifact on services_hosts.sh, diagnosed in the previous commit's evidence.
verifier: lib/tests/run_all.sh (222 assertions), an A/B of check_midnight_shutdown against a disabled+inactive timer with and without the guards, bash meta/scripts/shell_coverage.sh lib/tests/run_all.sh services_units.sh 100, grep for unguarded sites, shellcheck, and check_file_length.sh --all.
